transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’ve been having this thing late at night where I start picking at leftovers, and then I just keep going. Part of me is saying, “That’s enough, Alejandro,” but I still reach for more anyway.
When this happens, do you feel unable to stop eating once you’ve started?
Yes. Once I start, I tell myself I’ve had enough, but I keep going back for more anyway. It feels like I can’t quite make myself stop.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food for the situation?

Yes. I’ll be putting away tamales or mole after supper and end up eating several servings, then pan dulce too—usually out in the garage. It’s more than I’d ever serve myself if my family were watching.
During these late-night episodes, are you eating even when you’re not physically hungry?
A lot of the time, no—I’ve already had a good dinner with everyone. But later I’m still opening containers and tasting one thing after another.
Do these late-night eating episodes upset you a lot?
Yes, it does. I still keep up with my errands and appointments and help around the house, but the next morning I feel sluggish, and honestly, not very proud of myself.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don’t. I just feel bad afterward, but I don’t do that.
Do these eating episodes usually happen after you’ve been asleep and then wake up?
I’m not sure I’ve really noticed whether it’s after I’ve been asleep or not. I just know it tends to be late at night.
When these eating episodes happen, have you usually just woken up from sleep?
I honestly can’t say for sure. I haven’t paid attention to whether I’d been asleep first or if I was just still awake late.
When these late-night eating episodes happen, have you usually woken up from sleep just before you start eating?
I really haven’t noticed a pattern like that. Sometimes it’s just late, and I can’t say whether I’d been asleep right before or not.
When these late-night eating episodes happen, are you fully awake and aware of what you’re doing?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to how awake or aware I am at the time.
When you eat late at night like this, are you aware that you’re eating while it’s happening?
I’m not sure, to be honest. I haven’t really stopped to notice whether I’m fully aware of it while it’s happening.
Before one of these late-night eating episodes starts, have you usually just woken up from sleep?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I’d just woken up before it starts.
The next time this happens, does it usually start after you wake up from sleep?
I really couldn’t say. I haven’t noticed whether I wake up first or if it starts some other way.
During these late-night episodes, do you eat what most people would consider a very large amount of food?

Yeah. Some nights after supper, when I’m putting the tamales or mole away, I’ll eat several servings, then pan dulce too—usually out in the garage. It’s more than I’d ever put on a plate if my family were watching.
On a typical night when this happens, do you wake up from sleep before you start eating?
I don’t know, honestly. I haven’t paid attention to whether I wake up first on those nights.
When these episodes happen, do you first wake up from sleep and then start eating?
I’m not sure. I really haven’t noticed whether I wake up first or just end up eating later at night.
The next morning, do you usually remember the late-night eating clearly?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid attention to how much I remember the next morning.
Do these eating episodes ever start after you wake up from sleep?
I can’t say for sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I wake up and then start eating.
The next morning, do you clearly remember what you ate during these late-night episodes?
I honestly couldn’t tell you clearly. I haven’t really kept track of what I ate or how well I remember it the next day.
The next morning after one of these episodes, do you remember the eating clearly?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid close enough attention the next morning to know how clearly I remember it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent episodes of eating an unusually large amount of food with a subjective loss of control, often when not physically hungry, followed by marked distress/guilt and no compensatory vomiting. Night eating syndrome (F50.4) was considered because episodes occur late at night, but key features needed to support that diagnosis—such as eating after awakening from sleep, clear awareness/recall, and a consistent nocturnal pattern—were not established. Therefore the presentation is better captured as other specified eating disorder consistent with binge-eating-type symptoms.

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent late-night episodes of eating an unusually large amount of food for the situation
Subjective loss of control during episodes, reporting inability to stop once started
Eating despite not being physically hungry after already having dinner
Episodes associated with shame/distress and feeling 'not very proud' afterward

additional_requirements: No evidence obtained that episodes reliably follow awakening from sleep
Awareness during episodes was not confirmed
Recall of nocturnal eating the next morning was not confirmed
